utterances.text: And were you in a position to verify what General Rose said about that, because he writes about that in his book. He says that they fired outside the safe area and burned many Serb villages east of the Drina. Is that your own experience or not?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I have not been able to see for myself, and neither was I in a position to have UNMOs in the area. General Rose had at his disposal his own British personnel which he deployed, and maybe on the basis of that he concluded -- again, I'll allow General Rose to say, but I was not in a position, as Chief of Staff, to have my people there on the spot to make observations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you as the Chief of Staff know what the commander knew?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I'm not saying that in all cases I knew exactly what General Rose knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And is it true, General, that on the 9th of April, 1994, in the hangar of the Sarajevo airport, there was a joint meeting attended also by the American envoy Redmond?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It's possible, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend that meeting at that time?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I cannot remember whether there was such a discussion or whether I was present. I'd have to look at my notes from that period to see what happened. I can't remember offhand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, from General Rose's book, it emerges that Redmond --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't know if there's much point asking the witness about a meeting which he can't remember if he was at or not. Better ask General Rose about these things or call him to give evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was assuming, Mr. May, that General van Baal, as the Chief of Staff, knows what General Rose knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've heard his evidence about it. Now, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Izetbegovic at the time rejected the agreement that had been proposed on the 9th of April at the Sarajevo airport?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are familiar with the Dayton Accords?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that it coincides in many respects with the agreement that was proposed in 1994 when you were the Chief of Staff and which Izetbegovic rejected, as suggested by Redmond?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I'm trying to answer your questions as accurately as I can, but it's about the period that I was Chief of Staff in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Dayton Accords are about 1995. I can't improvise an answer and make a comparison between an agreement of 1994 about Gorazde and the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And is it true that you, on the 10th of April, 1994, after General Rose returned from Split, informed him that tanks of the army of Republika Srpska were at the approaches to Gorazde, and they were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. directly targeting buildings in the town and that villages in the neighbourhood were burning? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: When General Rose returned, I informed him of all the information I had at my disposal at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in your statement, you say that Serb tanks were targeting the hospital in Gorazde and that they hit it several times. You say this on page 7, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Yes. Afterwards I was able to see that the reports that reached us then were based on truth. I was able to observe that personally in Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally establish that they had hit the hospital and targeted it?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I observed this personally during my visit to Gorazde in the company of the local Muslim authorities and the UNPROFOR troops that were there at the time, and that confirmed earlier reports made by the United Nations military observers. One of the military observers, after he came back to Gorazde, I spoke to personally and he confirmed the reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is it, however, true that in the immediate vicinity of the hospital there were several mortar positions of the Muslim forces? You must have been able to establish that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That was reported as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it then clear that forces of the army of Republika Srpska were targeting firing positions that were being used to attack them and not the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I cannot confirm or deny that. What I did observe is that the hospital had been hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And the safe area was 3 kilometres from the centre of town, wasn't it? That was how it was establish.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That was established after a cease-fire was announced. In Resolution 836, the safe area of Gorazde is mentioned, and both parties were informed that the safe area of Gorazde covered an area of about 300 square kilometres. Finally, the Serb military officers brought all people and civilians from Gorazde back within a radius of 3 kilometres. That was the final agreement. The fighting took place before that agreement was reached, and the shooting of the hospital also occurred before the agreement was reached. But the safe area of Gorazde, in accordance with 836, covers an area of about 300 square kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is 3 kilometres from the centre of town; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In the final agreement an area was determined which all -- where all parties would refrain from fighting within a 3 kilometre radius from the centre of the city, and that is right. But that was after the area had been reduced from 300 square kilometres to about 27 square kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Was that after the NATO airstrike or before it? Airstrike on positions of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It was after. The agreement was signed afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, since these airstrikes were carried out on positions of the army of Republika Srpska in order allegedly to destroy the tanks that were in the prohibited areas, do you know how many tanks were destroyed in those airstrikes, tanks that had allegedly fired at Gorazde?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Tanks were moving towards Gorazde and were effectively firing. The NATO airstrikes were not very effective in the sense of destroying tanks, as far as I know, but they had the effect that a conversation could take place between General Mladic and UNPROFOR to reach an agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that an ambulance was destroyed and not a single tank because there were no tanks in that area? The airstrike was absolutely unjustified. There was no cause for it.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I saw a photograph showing signs of an ambulance being hit. It was not clear what projectile had hit it, and the rumour was that this had been caused by the deployment of NATO forces, but I did not get any confirmation of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, and I'm quoting from General Rose's book: "On Wednesday the 13th of April, many guests came accompanied by Lord Owen and Stoltenberg who were handed updated reports by the observers from the spot, and they believed that the activities were directed against the heights around town and the main road leading in and out of the valley. Contrary to the propaganda and reports, the Serbs did not target civilian targets, but they did seriously jeopardise the positions of the Muslim army in town." This is what General Rose says, that the Serbs did not target civilian facilities. Do you know that, General Van Baal?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I [Realtime transcript read in error "believe"] will leave that to the author of the book, General Rose. What I observed was that during the Gorazde crisis, there were hundreds of casualties and wounded. They were not [as interpreted] caused by a Serb attack on Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We all did our very best and used our influence for the conflicts around Gorazde to come to an end. There were messages coming from all sides if you remember that. I'm sure you do. And appeals addressed towards the parties to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It did not prove effective.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. General Van Baal, on page 8, paragraph 3, you say that "After the crisis in Gorazde, there was a meeting at the Sarajevo airport between Haris Silajdzic and Momcilo Krajisnik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's right. And I accompanied Mr. Silajdzic to the airport and back into town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. And is it true that at one of your meetings with Silajdzic you asked whether it was possible to transfer people from the eastern enclaves to the territory of the Federation?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I asked him that informally on returning from the airport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. On page 8, paragraph 3, you say that he answered: "We are the victims of the war. We enjoy the sympathy of the international community and the strong support of the United States. We are now going for the gold medal." Is that right, General?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't this a quite unambiguous option in favour of war, to sacrifice one's own people to win over the support of the part of the world that calls itself the international community?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's purely your comment. No doubt if we come to consider it if it's of any significance, we will have to consider what weight to give to it if any, but that's not a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness, in his statement, says that Silajdzic told him that he has the strong support of the United States and that he was going for the gold medal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And the witness has confirmed that. The witness has confirmed that is what he said. Now, what interpretation to put upon it, we may have to decide in due course if it is of any significance. Now, let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say at the end of that paragraph that I partly quoted from: "It was obvious that he expected military support from the United States." Is that right, General?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they got that military support, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Bosnia's Muslim government received political and military support, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. On page 9, in paragraph 6 of your statement, and also in your examination-in-chief today, you mentioned sniping activities, and then you say that you believe that the authority in the army of Republika Srpska for sniping came absolutely from the highest place. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's right. I also deduct that from the conversation with General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction; Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on what grounds do you believe that -- and you say that you believe that the authority for sniping came from the absolutely highest position in Republika Srpska. What led you to believe that?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: First of all, General Milovanovic stated that very clearly to me. If UNPROFOR allows trams to drive in Sarajevo, they show that there is peace in Sarajevo. There is no question of that. The Bosnian Serb side, the buses should drive, and that's a totally incorrect picture, because in the rest of the country war is going on, and I'll make sure that passengers will be shot at, and that also happened. At other times, I had a similar -- had a similar conversation with General Milovanovic where he indicated that he was able to mobilise the snipers or to have the snipers' activity ceased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. General -- very well, General. Will you please focus on what you say on the same page, paragraph 3 of your statement, when you talk about Muslim snipers, and I am quoting you: "There were snipers acting from the facilities of the Bosnian government." Did you say that? And I am quoting you literally: "There were snipers operating from facilities of the Bosnian government."

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: It was observed by UNPROFOR soldiers of sector Sarajevo, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. Since this is a quite unambiguous statement, that there were snipers operating from within Bosnian government buildings, isn't it illogical that you should accuse the Serb side on the basis of your belief that the decision about sniping came from the highest position, whereas in the case of Muslims who were killing Serbs from Bosnian government buildings, which you were able to establish as a fact on the ground, and you have absolute proof that their snipers are operating following instructions from the highest position as they're operating from the very buildings where that highest authority is housed.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: The question you are asking me -- the question you asked me was, first of all, about the Serb -- Bosnian Serb snipers. In my statement, I indicated that also the Bosnian Muslim side used snipers. There too, the central military authority was informed. There was observed by centre Sarajevo. I did not observe this myself. These were reports that sector Sarajevo made to my headquarters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's the time for us to adjourn. Have you any more questions for this witness, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Could we get through them in five or ten minutes, try and finish the witness today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'll finish so as not to keep the general here until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, General, let us just specify this point. Your conviction regarding sniping when referring to the Serbs, you express a conviction that the decisions came from the highest position, whereas on the other side you have very precise information that sniping is being done from Bosnian government buildings, and then you do not qualify them in the same manner, that is that sniping is being commanded and ordered from the highest positions, sniping against Serbs. Why? Is it important to accuse the Serbs, General?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: On the subject of the snipers, I spoke with General Milovanovic in person regarding snipers on the Bosnian Serb -- Muslim side. I did not speak with leaders of the Bosnian Muslim government. That's the difference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you're not going to say that General Milovanovic told you that they, from the top places, were deciding about snipers.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: General Milovanovic told me that if we made the trams -- if UNPROFOR allowed the trams to drive in Sarajevo, that he would have the trams be shot at. That's what he said literally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he did not say that he would use snipers. He said that he was asking for reciprocity, namely, that if trams were operating on the Muslim side, that there should be buses operating on the Serb side. If the trams were safe, then the buses should be safe too. He did not tell you that he would use snipers. Isn't that right, General?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Technically speaking, it was only possible with long-bearing small-calibre weapons, that is sniper rifles, to be able to reach the trams. That's a technical issue. The second point is that it did not only concern the fact having the trams drive combined with supplying spare parts and fuel for the buses, but he would like to stress that it was a wrong sign to the international community to have the trams drive and to have a picture that there was peace, and in other parts of the country there was a struggle going on. And so there were two arguments, and technically, shooting the trams from the Serb positions was only possible with long-range small-calibre arms because other weapons were not allowed in that zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I just wanted it to be established that General Milovanovic was talking to you about reciprocity there, trams and buses. He wasn't talking about snipers. He never mentioned any snipers; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: He talked about shooting the trams.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He did not mention snipers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think there's much point going on with the argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in great detail, you exercised control over the exclusion of the heavy weaponry of the army of Republika Srpska from the total exclusion zone around Sarajevo. Why could you not exclude the heavy weaponry that you yourself said the Muslim forces had near the airport and near the hospital? Why didn't you exclude that heavy weaponry?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: Regarding the hospital, heavy weaponry were placed in a tunnel, near the tunnel. We did not have any access of UNPROFOR. We observed that had when I arrived in Sarajevo, and this did not change during my term. Heavy mortars in the neighbourhood of the airport, these were mobile, so we never even found them, but we observed that they had been used to fire mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understood from what you were saying that you have not read General Rose's book about his mission in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I did read the book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well then, since you read the book, tell me whether you agree with Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. what he said. In his book, on page 304, in the afterward - I could quote a greet many other things but I'm just going to read what you told me you've already read yourself - so General Rose says: "I was especially angry at the journalists because of their partial unobjective reporting from Bosnia. Most of the commentators from the east coast of the US during the fighting in Gorazde in 1994 did not write about the misfortune and the difficult economic position of the population. Rather, they talked about torched and destroyed houses. However, the truth was different. These houses that American reconnaissance planes were filming during airstrikes against the Serbs were destroyed for the most part as far as back as 1992 when the Serbs and Muslims were fighting for supremacy in town and when --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Pause there. The witness should have a chance to answer. Can you make any comment at all, General, on what General Rose has said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Rose I know from several moments was worried about the impartiality of a number of journalists, but it was established that General Rose realised that some journalists did not have access to Republika Srpska and had to use the possibilities in and around Sarajevo. So he understood that these people had a view, but the possibilities were lacking to gather information, and he expressed his concern about this several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you see what he says at this point where Mr. May interrupted me. He says that American reconnaissance planes were filming and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, there's not really much point going on with this. What you're asking is a witness to comment on what somebody else has said, somebody else's opinions, and in any event, what does it matter -- just a moment. What does it matter, as far as this trial is concerned, whether the witness -- the journalists were biased or not? They're not giving any evidence. We're not relying on what they said. So it doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here he refers to American reconnaissance planes, aircraft, not journalists. And the point is that he continues to say these were Serb houses without windowpanes, without door frames, et cetera, that the Muslim have completely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Look, there is no point asking this witness about what General Rose has said. Now you may have the chance if you want to call him. You can call him to give evidence, if that's what you want to say. Now, time is really short. Is there anything more you want to ask the General, any other topic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Van Baal, is this your conviction too? What was represented as victims on the side of the Muslims were actually Serb houses that had been destroyed and torched by the Muslim side, and that was what was being shown in order to justify through the media the policy of aggression against the Serb side. Is that right or is that not right, General?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: I have no comments to this general statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kay. Questioned by Mr. Kay:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a very short matter, General. Firstly, you had dealings with Dr. Radovan Karadzic on a personal level; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: No. That was on a functional level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I missed that because I --

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: No. That was on a functional level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You misunderstand me. What I'm saying is that you had dealings while carrying out your job with Dr. Karadzic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your dealings with Dr. Karadzic, he exerted control over the issues that you asked him to respond to?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he made it clear that he was the leader of the Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in relation to General Mladic, again you had dealings with that General who was commander of the Bosnian Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was clear to you that he exerted control over those forces.

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: One matter of clarification if I may. It's the question that was raised on the screen I can see, 13:37 and thereabouts. Re-examined by Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you were asked in respect of something that General Rose is said to have written in his books -- his book, I beg your pardon, about the Serbs not targeting civilian targets in Gorazde. And you were asked a question that included General Rose saying that they did nevertheless seriously jeopardise the position of the Muslim army in town. Your answer, and I'll just read your answer in full and see if it's been correctly recorded. It's as follows. It says: "I will believe," but it means "I will leave that to the author of the book, General Rose. What I observed was that during the Gorazde crisis there were hundreds of casualties and wounded." And the next sentence reads: "They were not caused by a Serb attack on Gorazde." First of all, is that the answer you intended to give?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: What I meant to say, it was the consequence of a Serb attack on Gorazde. Apparently the word "not" was put in. The wounded and casualties caused in the Gorazde crisis were caused by a Serb attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think the only other question, Your Honour, that I'd like to ask is this: You've explained already but I want to be quite sure we understand it, Mladic's pressure for a total cease-fire, something rejected throughout by the Muslims, if -- if they'd yielded to it, what would have been the effect of the total cease-fire and demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: ADRIANUS VAN BAAL
utterances.text: In fact, a one-sided disarmament, and the Muslim-Croatian Federation would have been weakened, and it would have been a simple walkover to Republika Srpska. That would have been the consequence, and that is what General Delic stressed, "I will be unprotected if I yield to this one-sided disarmament."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: General, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are now free to go. And we will adjourn until to tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Responding to your earlier request in respect of information about Brcko, so far the best official publication I can find for you is the 2001 publication on the website by the Office of the High Representative. I think it contains the facts in the penultimate two paragraphs, contains a certain amount of description as well. I've checked that there has been nothing material that's happened since then. The arbitration award referred to here is still in effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd hand it in. Yes. We will adjourn.
